app.analyticsHelpAria: How it's computed and what it means

attendance.formula: Days worked ÷ scheduled days, across all active employees for the period.
attendance.meaning: How reliably people show up overall. 100% means everyone worked every scheduled day.
attendance.improve: Follow up with the people who miss a lot of days (the "Needs attention" list below). Check the schedules are right and that everyone knows checking in is required.

avgHours.formula: Total hours worked ÷ number of days worked (from check-in data).
avgHours.meaning: How long an average working day runs. Compare it to the expected shift length.
avgHours.improve: If it's low, people leave early or don't close their shift on time. If it's high, that's overtime or shifts closed late.

late.formula: Days with a late arrival ÷ days worked, across all employees.
late.meaning: How often people arrive after the shift start. What counts as late is set in attendance settings.
late.improve: Talk to the people listed below. Make sure the shift start time in the schedule matches reality.

early.formula: Days with an early leave ÷ days worked.
early.meaning: How often people leave before the shift ends.
early.improve: If it fires for almost everyone, the threshold probably doesn't match the real shift end — fix it in settings. Otherwise handle it case by case.

geo.formula: Days where the check-in was confirmed by location ÷ days worked.
geo.meaning: Share of check-ins made on site (the browser confirmed coordinates). Low means either you don't require location or people don't grant access.
geo.improve: Turn on required location on check-in and ask employees to allow browser location access.

openShift.formula: Days where someone checked in but never checked out and the shift didn't auto-close ÷ days worked.
openShift.meaning: How often people forget to check out. Those days are counted wrong and distort the hours.
openShift.improve: Remind people to check out. Set up shift auto-close so forgotten shifts don't break the stats.

contacts.integrationSteps_kcell:
Open the Kcell virtual PBX account, the CRM integration section.
Paste the address above into the CRM address field.
Make a test call: the integration status becomes “Working”.
contacts.integrationSteps_gravitel:
In the PBX account open the CRM integration and set the address above as the CRM address.
The history, event and client commands are appended automatically.
Make a test call: the status becomes “Working”.
contacts.integrationSteps_zadarma:
In Zadarma open Settings → Integrations and API → Notifications.
Paste the address above and enable the call notifications you need.
Take the API key and secret from the same section and save them here.
contacts.integrationSteps_mango:
In the Mango Office account open the API settings.
Set the address above for call events, summaries and recordings.
Enter the PBX code and signing key here. The adapter has not been verified on a live account yet.
contacts.integrationSteps_universal:
Configure the PBX or a script to POST lota-format requests to the address above.
Sign the body with the secret in the X-Lota-Signature header: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256>.
Events: started, accepted, ended, history, recording, rating and contact (client name lookup).
